==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|lett||archaic}} * {{alt|en|lettest||2nd person singular simple present and simple past; archaic}} * {{alt|en|letteth||3rd person singular simple present; archaic}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/lɛt/}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-let.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{audio|en|en-us-let.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛt|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|Lett}} ===Etymology 1=== {{der+|en|enm|leten}}, {{m|enm|læten}}, from {{der|en|ang|lǣtan||to allow, let go, bequeath, leave, rent}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*lātan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lētaną||to leave behind, allow}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*leh₁d-||to be tired, leave}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|lat}}, {{m|sco|lete||to let, leave}}, {{cog|yol|leth||let}}, {{cog|frr|leet}}, {{m|frr|let}}, {{m|frr|lätje||to let}}, {{cog|bar|låssn||to let}}, {{cog|nl|-}}, {{cog|nds|laten||to let, leave}}, {{cog|de|lassen}}, {{m|de|laßen||to let, leave, allow}}, {{cog|lb|loossen||to let, leave}}, {{cog|yi|לאָזן||to let}}, {{cog|da|lade||to let, allow, leave}}, {{cog|fo|-}}, {{cog|is|láta||to let}}, {{cog|nb|la||to let, leave}}, {{cog|nn|la}}, {{m|nn|lata}}, {{m|nn|late||let, allow}}, {{cog|sv|låta||to let, allow, leave}}, {{cog|got|𐌻𐌴𐍄𐌰𐌽||to let}}, {{cog|sq|lë||to allow, let, leave}} and partially related to [[French]] {{m|fr|laisser||to let}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ting|~,leet|+,~ten}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[allow]] to, not to prevent {{qualifier|+ infinitive, but usually without {{m|en|to}}}}. #: {{ux|en|After he knocked for hours, I decided to '''let''' him come in.}} #: {{ux|en|I never '''let''' myself worry about the future.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Exodus|8|28|passage=Pharaoh said, I will '''let''' you go.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Hamlet|act=IV|scene=vi|passage=If your name be Horatio, as I am '''let''' to know it is{{...}}}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1971|author=w:Ursula K. Le Guin|title=w:The Tombs of Atuan |passage=He could not be '''let''' die of thirst there alone in the dark.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman| volume=189| issue=2| page=27| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google The tao of tech]| passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that '''let''' you "stay up to date with what your friends are doing",{{...}}and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To allow to be or do without interference; to not disturb or meddle with; to [[leave alone]]. #: {{ux|en|'''Let''' me be!}} #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=VI|stanza=16|passage=Yet neither spinnes nor cardes, ne cares nor frets, / But to her mother Nature all her care she '''lets'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To allow the release of (a fluid). #: {{ux|en|The physicians '''let''' about a pint of his blood, but to no avail.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|chiefly|British}} To allow possession of (a property etc.) in exchange for [[rent]]. #: {{ux|en|I decided to '''let''' the farmhouse to a couple while I was working abroad.}} #* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|volume=I|chapter=I|pages=1–2|passage=“My dear Mr. Bennet,” said his lady to him one day, “have you heard that Netherfield Park is '''let''' at last?”
Mr. Bennet replied that he had not.
“But it is,” returned she; “for Mrs. Long has just been here, and she told me all about it.”}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To give, grant, or assign, as a work, privilege, or contract; often with ''out''. #: {{ux|en|to '''let''' the building of a bridge;  to '''let''' out the lathing and the plastering}} # {{lb|en|auxiliary|transitive}} {{non-gloss|Used to introduce a first or third person imperative verb construction.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Let''''s put on a show!}} #: {{ux|en|'''Let''' us have a moment of silence.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Let''' me just give you the phone number.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Let''' ''P'' be the point where ''AB'' and ''OX'' intersect.}} #: {{ux|en|"'''Let''' there be no doubt: I saw your boyfriend with another girl" "'''Let''' him, [[see if I care]]!".}} #: {{ux|en|'''Let''' the show go on!}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete|_|except with [[know]] or [[be]]}} To [[cause]] {{qualifier|+ bare infinitive}}. #: {{ux|en|Can you '''let''' me know what time you'll be arriving?}} #* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|6.4|2|IV|iv|passage=Soo within a whyle kynge Pellinore cam with a grete hoost and salewed the peple and the kyng and ther was grete ioye made on euery syde. Thenne the kyng '''lete''' serche how moche people of his party ther was slayne. And ther were founde but lytel past two honderd men slayne and viij knyȝtes of the table round in their pauelions.|t=So after a while King Pellinore came with a great host and saluted the people and the king, and there was great joy on every side. Then the king '''let''' search how many people of his faction were slain. And there were found only a little more than two hundred men slain, and eight knights of the Table Round in their pavilions.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1818|author=w:John Keats|title=To— |passage=Time's sea hath been five years at its slow ebb, / Long hours have to and fro '''let''' creep the sand{{nb...}}.}} #* {{RQ:Thoreau Walden|chapter=The Ponds|page=212|passage=What right had the unclean and stupid farmer, whose farm abutted on this sky water, whose shores he has ruthlessly laid bare, to give his name to it? ... Rather '''let''' it be named from the fishes that swim in it, the wild fowl or quadrupeds which frequent it, the wild flowers which grow by its shores, or some wild man or child the thread of whose history is interwoven with its own...}} =====Usage notes===== * The use of “let” to introduce an imperative may sometimes be confused with its use, ''as its own imperative'', in the sense of “to allow”. For example, the sentence “'''Let''' me go to the store.” could either be a second-person imperative of “let” (addressing someone who might prevent the speaker from going to the store) or a first-person singular imperative of “go” (not implying any such preventer). =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|to allow}} {{l|en|allow}}, {{l|en|permit}} =====Derived terms===== ===Etymology 2=== {{der+|en|enm|letten||to hinder, delay}}, from {{der|en|ang|lettan||to hinder, delay”; literally, “to make late}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*lattjan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*latjaną}}. Akin to {{cog|ang|latian||to delay}}, {{cog|nl|letten}}, {{cog|ang|læt||late}}. More at [[late]], [[delay]]. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|+|~}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} To [[hinder]], [[prevent]], [[impede]], [[hamper]], [[cumber]]; to [[obstruct]] {{gl|someone or something}}. #* {{RQ:King James Version|2 Thessalonians|2|7|passage=He who now '''letteth''' will '''let''', until he be taken out of the way.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson Idylls|page=152|passage=Sir King, mine ancient wound is hardly whole, / And '''lets''' me from the saddle; {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[prevent]] someone from doing something; also to [[prevent]] something from happening. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1485|author=w:Thomas Malory|title={{w|Le Morte Darthur}} Book XXI, Chapter ii, [https://quod.lib.umich.edu/c/cme/MaloryWks2/1:23.2?rgn=div2;view=fulltext leaf 421r]|text=''& there was syr Mordred redy awaytynge vpon his londage to '''lette''' his owne fader to lāde vp the lande that he was kyng ouer.''
"And there was Sir Mordred ready awaiting upon his landing, to '''let''' his own father to land upon the land that he was king over."}} #* {{RQ:Tyndale NT|Acts|8|passage=And as they went on their waye, they cam unto a certayne water, and the gelded man sayde: Se here is water, what shall '''lett''' me to be baptised?}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[tarry]] or [[delay]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1826|section=The History of Sir Eger, Sir Grahame, And Sir Gray-Steel|title=Early Metrical Tales; Including the History of Sir Egeir, Sir Gryme, and Sir Gray-Steill|location=Edinburgh|page=7|passage=And for that strake I would not '''let''', / Another upon him soon I set, {{...}}}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|or|legal}} An [[obstacle]] or [[hindrance]]. #: {{ux|en|without '''let''' or hindrance}} #* {{RQ:Latimer Sermons|volume=II|sermon=XXV|chapter=Preached on the Twenty First Sunday after Trinity|date=12 June 1552|page=541|passage=[E]ver conſider vvhether our doings be to the '''let''' of our ſalvation or not.}} #* {{RQ:Ovid Golding Metamorphosis|book=3|lines=60–61|passage=And Cadmus saw his campanie make tarience in that sort / He marveld what should be their '''let''', and went to seeke them out.}} #* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=16|book=II|passage=''Paulus Emilius'' going to the glorious expedition of ''Macedon'', advertised the people of ''Rome'' during his absence not to speake of his actions: ''For the licence of judgements is an especiall '''let''' in great affaires.''}} # {{lb|en|tennis}} The [[hindrance]] caused by the [[net]] during [[serve]], only if the ball falls legally. =====Derived terms===== * {{l|en|without let or hindrance}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|hindrance}} * Portuguese: * Serbo-Croatian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|hindrance caused by the net during serve at tennis}} * French: * German: * Māori: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== * [http://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/dost/let_v The Dictionary of the Scots Language] ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=elt|ELT|ETL|LTE|TEL|TLE|Tel.|elt|tel}} {{cln|en|irregular past participles|irregular simple past forms|irregular verbs}}
